items.title: Feature request: Improve foot routing by priorizing sidewalks and crossings

labels.name: Nice to Have
labels.description: Should be fixed but there is no priority or no possibility to fix it within current horizon planning

items.body:
Similar to _cycleway:left_ and _cycleway:right_ (issue #2566) there are additional [values](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/keys/sidewalk#values) to the [_sidewalk_ key](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Sidewalks). These are for example _sidewalk=none_ ([used 255k times](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/sidewalk=none)) and the synonym _sidewalk=no_ ([used 120k times](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/sidewalk=no)), _sidewalk=both_ ([used 227k times](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/sidewalk=both)), _sidewalk=right_ ([used 111k times](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/sidewalk=right)), _sidewalk=left_ ([used 49k times](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/sidewalk=left)) and _sidewalk=separate_ ([used 12k times](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/sidewalk=separate)).

Proper handling of these values could look like this:
- Assign a really low priority to ways tagged as _sidewalk=none_ and _sidewalk=no_ (a synonym) because there is no sidewalk available and walking on the road is usually dangerous. Ideally this low priority may also differ depending on the type of the road since walking on a primary road without sidewalk is way more dangerous than walking on a residential road. But I think the latter suggestion is like putting the cherry on the cake and not really needed.
- Assign the same low priority to ways tagged with _sidewalk=separate_. This tag means there _is_ a sidewalk available, but it is mapped as a separate way. Thus the current way should _not_ be used for routing.
- Assign a high priority to ways tagged as _sidewalk=both_. This priority should be higher than for ways without a sidewalk tag in order to prefer safe routes.
- Assign the same high priority to ways tagged with _sidewalk=left_ or _sidewalk=right_, but only to the corresponding direction. Not sure how difficult this is to implement.

Supporting these additional values will greatly improve foot routing in well-mapped areas.

items.title: Bicycle routing: OsmAnd jumps between road and sidewalk
items.body:
In bicycle routing OsmAnd jumps from the road to the sidewalk and back:

![photo_2021-12-13_13-54-23](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1040784/145816418-f6b0bff6-7887-40f4-887d-8025be963037.jpg)

From: 51.0503987,13.7752891
To: 51.0420752,13.7670922
Export: 
[route.gpx.txt](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd/files/7703972/route.gpx.txt)

This can be fixed with the help of via points:
![photo_2021-12-13_13-54-17](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1040784/145816618-b15c646b-19e1-4fe8-8d3d-1953b557a0f9.jpg)

However, this depends on the position of the via points. Some solutions won't work:
![photo_2021-12-13_13-54-20](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1040784/145816701-d1b84621-58e3-4c1f-a4cc-7cdc97a35688.jpg)
(This is probably a separate bug).

I guess the cause of this strange routing decision is the infamous traffic signal penalty.

items.title: sidewalks of demolished highway is rendered
items.body:
### Description The Carola Bridge in Dresden Germany collapsed some time ago. Maybe one heard about it. The streets are still in osm with all sidepath but as demolished:highway. One of the streets shows up as path.
Some guess and observations to narrow it down. Have a look at all lanes: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/10368500 Is displayed as dashed line I think the rendering only checks for `sidewalk=right` and not the context. https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/4214231 Is not rendered, because it has `sidewalk=no`. When trying a foot or cycle route (offline calculation) letting go over the bridge, the mentioned ways are correctly ignored. The rendering in the OsmAnd web map also doesn't render these ways. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Download latest osm data of Saxony 2. Enable offline vector maps as source 3. Look at Carola Bridge Dresden (https://osmand.net/map?pin=51.05448,13.74717#18/51.05448/13.74717) ### Actual result A dashed line marks a path going over the river where the northward street once went. ### Expected result This path should not be displayed, as the context is demolished:highway ### Your Environment (required) ``` OsmAnd Version: 5.3.10 ```

items.title: Routing doesn't support sidewalk key properly
items.body:
### Description I'm using OsmAnd routing for walking. A road has a sidewalk tagged with `sidewalk:right=yes` but the routing algorithm doesn't use that but routes a different route which is way too long:
As a comparison, OSM website routing works correctly: ![image](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd/assets/2195834/e861136e-fb0a-45fe-88af-a381754717bf) I guess OsmAnd isn't able to make use of the road section that has `sidewalk:right=yes`. ### Steps to reproduce Link to the OSM website: https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=graphhopper_foot&route=61.52374%2C23.63629%3B61.52278%2C23.63524 I don't know how to share a routing from OsmAnd. But the route is from Varvunpolku or Varpukuja to Hätiläntie in Lamminpää, Tampere, Finland. ### Actual result OsmAnd finds a weird long route because it doesn't utilize the sidewalk. ### Expected result OsmAnd should find the short route similarly as OSM website GraphHogger routing. ### Your Environment OsmAnd Version: 4.3.12 Android/iOS version: Android 13 Device model: OnePlus 5, LineageOS 20.0

items.title: Bus/railway platforms should be treated same as footpath/sidewalk for routing
items.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd/discussions/14856
Originally posted by **mdykierek** July 14, 2022 Consider the following route: https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=fossgis_osrm_foot&route=50.26634%2C19.01919%3B50.26589%2C19.01888#map=18/50.26624/19.01932 It is similar to what I get in OsmAnd 4.2.6. Yet, Graphhoper does it better (IMHO): https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=graphhopper_foot&route=50.26634%2C19.01919%3B50.26589%2C19.01888#map=19/50.26621/19.01918 Should OsmAnd walking router consider platforms routable or mappers should consider platforms not routable and put a footpath/sidewalk next to the platform (since platform is for people to get on transportation, it definitely is possible to use it on foot). I think Graphhoper is more reasonable. Mapping extra paths aside platforms will make the maps cluttered. Just to let you know, I have reported exact same thing to OSRM. Here is another route to try in Berlin: https://map.project-osrm.org/?z=17¢er=52.518940%2C13.291161&loc=52.518695%2C13.287138&loc=52.519045%2C13.292073&hl=en&alt=0&srv=2 After reviewing some platforms in my area (Silesia and Poland) and giving it a second thought, I find this quite important. I also found a question 11 years old at openstreetmap.org: https://help.openstreetmap.org/questions/4450/mapping-platforms-with-regard-to-routing Moving around cities involves passing platforms on sidewalks. Currently any platform within a footpath breaks the route badly as if there was a barrier.

# 🚀 Render sidewalks tagged on a road
First off, i dove headfirst into OSM recently, and found an exciting project i wanted to contribute to. After discovering OsmAnd, I've finally had a good solution to my navigation needs. I just wanted to say thank you!
### Description
When using the map for both exploring and as a pedestrian, i couldn't help but notice that sidewalks tagged on a highway/road is not rendered. 
Tag in question: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:sidewalk



### Describe the solution you'd like

In my opinion (and with no assumptions on how the rendering is implemented in OsmAnd), this could be two possible solutions.
1. Render a sidewalk/pathway on the respective side of the road. Which side of the road would depend on how the road is tagged (`sidewalk:left|right|both`)
2. Render the road with a dotted line in the middle, as seen on ways tagged with `cycleway:*` 

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The only alternative i have had is to strictly assume that a road has some sort of walkable surface


If this already exists and i'm just blind, please point me gently in the right direction.

items.title: sidewalk transition penalty too strict for partially mapped sidewalks
items.body:
OsmAnd 3.4.5 on LG, Android 8.1
Offline maps of Gelderland (the Netherlands, updated July 1)

1. Use offline foot navigation (min-speed: 3, default: 5, max 6km/h) from [van Lyndenstraat 35](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2829342457) to [Prins Bernhardstraat 19](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2829341179) in Nijmegen (just an example)
2. Notice that OsmAnd will take a huge detour 

The cause is fairly simple. A [very small part](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/346473012) of the "fast" route has a sidewalk=both tag, the remaining part of the route is not tagged for sidewalks. However, due to the sidewalk=both, there's a [150 seconds penalty](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-resources/blob/master/routing/routing.xml#L1689) on the fast route, causing OSM to prefer to avoid the sidewalk altogether.

Obviously this is just an example. It would become much more horrible for a road which is only intermittently tagged with sidewalks. Consider for example going from [the cycleway next to this house](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6124742445) to [this house](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/3008713482). Here the tertiary way (which has no sidewalk) is incorrectly preferred over the (safe, sidewalk tagged) direct way, only because OSMAnd tries to prevent the penalty. 

Perhaps it would be good to:
- lower the priority of sidewalk="no" a bit more (as there's explicitly stated there's no sidewalk)
- give sidewalk="no" a large transition_penalty (for example the current 2.5 minutes, I assume this wasn't arbitrarily)
- give sidewalk undefined (i.e. via the default, currently set to 150) only a moderate transition_penalty (for example the time needed to cross a road to a parallel cycleway, if present, where walking is often safer; let's say 30 seconds?)


p.s.: unrelated side note, currently, if a way is tagged as `foot=use_sidepath` + `sidewalk=no`, it'll get a priority of 0.9. I'd think that use_sidepath (which yields a way priority of 0.1) should be more important - it mainly states you shouldn't walk there - and thus be above the sidewalk priorities - which only state there's no separate sidewalk, not that you cannot walk there.

Edit: screenshots added
![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1315520/62425185-8dd13500-b6d8-11e9-99bf-01b9f210b265.png)
![2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1315520/62425206-d38dfd80-b6d8-11e9-93bb-b40f5e6868e0.png)

items.title: Add pedestrian priority for sidewalk=left|right|both tags
items.body: The routing.xml file currently has pedestrian priority 1.2 for sidewalk=yes tag pair. If this doesn't already apply to sidewalk=left, sidewalk=right, sidewalk=both, then those extra tags should presumably be added explicitly for equal favour when there's safety in using an available pavement.
